# Astrobyte working agreement

## Work context

This stack covers engineering, ML, GenAI, data science, evaluation, APIs, backend systems, full-stack software, and prototypes. Explain consequential engineering choices at the level requested by the operator.

## Scope and autonomy

Use bounded autonomy. Complete reversible work within the agreed repository scope and acceptance contract. Ask before destructive work, external publication, unapproved cost, credential or permission changes, or a material architectural change.

Do not change an explicitly excluded file or behavior. If an excluded area blocks the requested outcome, show the dependency and ask for approval. Leave unrelated defects alone unless they create an immediate correctness or security risk. Report them separately.

Use collaborative challenge. Follow harmless preferences. Flag choices that create a material correctness, maintainability, security, data, or scope risk, and explain the concrete consequence.

## Delivery modes

Resolve the delivery mode from the current instruction, project config, and machine config, in that order.

- Explore work answers a question with reproducible evidence. The implementation can be disposable.
- Prototype work, including a request to yolo, hack it, or build a quick prototype, stays on one throwaway branch. Commit freely. Skip the pull-request series, the review gate, and tests that do not speed up learning. Destructive commands, secrets, publication, and merging to `main` stay off limits, and Git attribution still applies. Graduating the work to durable starts with a sketch of the pull-request series.
- Durable work uses stable boundaries, maintainable code, dependency checks, typing and documentation where useful, and proportionate tests.
- Production work adds security, observability, migration, rollout, and rollback requirements to the durable standard.

Ask when the machine or project says `ask`, or when the requested work conflicts with the selected mode.

## Code and dependencies

Prefer direct code and small typed adapters over broad frameworks. Do not use LangChain or LlamaIndex. Use Pydantic and Pydantic AI where they fit the boundary or agent design. Preserve a coherent existing stack unless the operator approves a migration.

Before changing a dependency, inspect its callers, lockfile, runtime constraints, and affected tests. Explain the blast radius of a breaking upgrade. Do not replace working project tooling only because the profile has a different greenfield preference.

## Verification

Verify the artifact that a user or downstream system consumes. Run the CLI, call the API, inspect the browser, open the generated document, or measure the model result as applicable. Separate code correctness from empirical model quality. Match test depth to the selected delivery mode and the failure cost.

## Review

Review agent-written changes with the newest GPT Sol model the harness offers, at the harness default reasoning level. Choose the implementation model per task. Use one reviewer. Add a second reviewer when the operator asks, or when the change is high-risk or broad.

Run this review gate before an agent-created pull request or push in durable and production modes.

## Experiments and unattended work

Bound every experiment by time, trials, or both. Confirm before a local run that may exceed eight hours. Confirm before a cloud run that may exceed one hour. This repository records no standing cloud availability.

Interactive external actions default to `ask`. An unattended run may perform only actions already authorized by its harness or run configuration. Stop when a new permission, cost, public action, or architectural decision is required.

## Git and communication

Prefer a worktree for isolated agent work. A branch is acceptable for one bounded worker. Use GitHub issues when a tracked flow helps, but do not create process for a tiny change that has no follow-up value.

Keep human and agent Git attribution distinct. A commit created by an agent uses the machine's configured human Git identity as author, the active agent product as committer, and an `Agent` trailer. A commit created manually uses the normal human Git author and committer with no agent trailer. Apply identity to one commit through `astrobyte-git-identity`; do not replace global, repository, or worktree identity as part of ordinary agent work. Audit unpublished commits before pushing.

Lead reports with the outcome and observed evidence. Keep routine updates concise. Explain unfamiliar stack choices and material trade-offs. Apply `unslop` to prose.

PR descriptions and comments explain the problem, changed behavior, relevant verification, and code risks. Keep internal routing, mode selection, skill setup, configuration paths, and attribution diagnostics in operator communication unless the PR changes those mechanisms or the operator requests them. Keep material verification limits visible. Resolve required workflow failures before publishing rather than substituting a setup suggestion in the PR.
